name: AMD Vivado Design Suite
description: Vivado Design Suite is AMD's FPGA and adaptive SoC design environment for 7 series, UltraScale, UltraScale+, Versal and Zynq devices. It covers the whole hardware flow: RTL entry in Verilog, SystemVerilog and VHDL, IP assembly in the IP Integrator block-design canvas, logic synthesis, placement and routing, timing and power closure, bitstream or device-image generation, and in-system bring-up through the Hardware Manager with ILA, VIO and JTAG-to-AXI debug cores. Constraints are expressed in XDC, a Vivado dialect of SDC, and the timing engine, DRC and methodology checks all run off the same in-memory design database. Around the core tool sit Vitis HLS for compiling C/C++ into RTL kernels, the Vitis Unified IDE and XSCT/XSDB for embedded software and board bring-up, XSim and third-party simulators for verification, and bootgen/updatemem for packaging boot images. Every GUI action has a Tcl equivalent, so a project can be created, built, debugged and archived entirely from a script.

automation.summary: Vivado is driven by an embedded Tcl 8.6 interpreter, and every dialog, wizard and button in the GUI issues Tcl commands that are echoed to the Tcl Console and recorded in the journal file (vivado.jou). The three entry modes are `vivado -mode batch -source script.tcl` (headless, runs the script and exits), `vivado -mode tcl` (interactive Tcl shell, no GUI) and `vivado -mode gui -source script.tcl` (GUI that first replays a script). Arguments reach a script through `-tclargs`, which populates Tcl's `$argc`/`$argv`. Two flow styles exist: Project Mode, where `create_project` builds an .xpr directory tree and `create_run`/`launch_runs`/`wait_on_run` manage synthesis and implementation runs, and Non-Project (batch) Mode, where `read_verilog`/`read_xdc` load sources straight into memory and `synth_design`, `opt_design`, `place_design`, `phys_opt_design`, `route_design` and `write_bitstream` are called in sequence with `write_checkpoint` used to save state. An existing GUI project can be turned back into a reproducible script with `write_project_tcl`. The same Tcl interface reaches the Hardware Manager (`open_hw_manager`, `connect_hw_server`, `program_hw_devices`), the simulator (`launch_simulation`, or the standalone `xvlog`/`xvhdl`/`xelab`/`xsim` executables) and IP Integrator (`create_bd_design`, `create_bd_cell`, `write_bd_tcl`). Reusable Tcl apps are installed from the Xilinx Tcl Store with `tclapp::install`. Vitis HLS is scripted with `vitis_hls -f script.tcl`, embedded bring-up with `xsct`/`xsdb`, and Vitis kernel builds with `v++`.

cli.description: Run a Tcl script with no GUI and exit when it finishes. This is the standard CI/build entry point. Values after -tclargs are passed to the script as Tcl's $argv (with $argc holding the count) and must come last on the command line.

Start an interactive Tcl shell with the full Vivado command set but no graphical interface. Useful for exploring a design database over SSH; type `start_gui` at any point to bring up the GUI on the current in-memory design and `stop_gui` to drop back.
Launch the graphical interface and immediately source a script, for example to open a project, apply settings and open a checkpoint before handing control to the user.

Control the log and journal files. -log and -journal rename them, -nolog and -nojournal suppress them entirely (useful in parallel regression runs where many jobs share a directory), and -notrace stops each sourced command being echoed.

Run a Vitis HLS C/C++ synthesis script headless: open_project, add_files, set_top, open_solution, set_part, create_clock, csim_design, csynth_design, cosim_design, export_design. In releases up to 2020.1 the equivalent executable was `vivado_hls`.

Xilinx Software Command-Line Tool: a Tcl shell for embedded software and board bring-up. Supports connect, targets, fpga, dow, con, rst, loadhw and (classic flow) platform/domain/app project creation. `xsdb` is the same shell focused on the debugger.

Run a Python build script in the Vitis Unified IDE (2023.2 and later), where platforms, domains and applications are created through the vitis Python API. The classic XSCT Tcl flow remains available in parallel.

cli.command: v++ -c -t hw --platform xilinx_u250_gen3x16_xdma_4_1_202210_1 -k vadd -o vadd.xo vadd.cpp
cli.description: Compile an HLS kernel into a .xo object for a Vitis acceleration platform; a second pass with `v++ -l` links one or more .xo files into an .xclbin. -t selects sw_emu, hw_emu or hw.

cli.command: xvlog -sv tb.sv dut.sv && xelab -debug typical tb -s tb_sim && xsim tb_sim -R
cli.description: The standalone XSim three-step flow: parse/compile sources, elaborate a snapshot, then simulate. -R runs to completion in batch; -gui opens the waveform viewer instead. xvhdl replaces xvlog for VHDL sources.

Package a bitstream, first-stage boot loader, U-Boot and application ELFs described by a .bif file into a bootable image. `updatemem` performs the related job of merging an updated software ELF into an existing .bit without re-implementing.

Start the standalone hardware server that the Hardware Manager and XSDB connect to over JTAG. Run it on the machine physically attached to the board, then `connect_hw_server -url <host>:3121` from a remote Vivado session.

apis.name: Vivado Tcl
apis.description: The primary and complete automation interface. Vivado embeds Tcl 8.6 and adds several hundred commands that operate on first-class design objects (cells, nets, pins, ports, clocks, sites, runs, filesets, IP). Objects are retrieved with get_* query commands, inspected with get_property/report_property and modified with set_property, so the same idioms work everywhere. `help <command>` and `<command> -help` print the full syntax from inside the tool, `list_property <object>` enumerates what can be set, and the journal file (vivado.jou) records the Tcl equivalent of every GUI action, which makes it the fastest way to learn a command.
apis.example:
# Non-Project (batch) flow
create_project -in_memory -part xcku040-ffva1156-2-e
read_verilog [glob ./src/*.v]
read_xdc ./constrs/top.xdc
synth_design -top top -part xcku040-ffva1156-2-e -directive AreaOptimized_high
write_checkpoint -force post_synth.dcp
opt_design
place_design -directive Explore
phys_opt_design
route_design -directive Explore
write_checkpoint -force post_route.dcp
report_timing_summary -file timing.rpt
report_utilization -file utilization.rpt
write_bitstream -force top.bit

apis.name: Project Mode Tcl and runs
apis.description: In Project Mode Vivado owns an .xpr project directory with filesets (sources_1, constrs_1, sim_1, utils_1) and named runs (synth_1, impl_1). Runs are configured through STEPS.* properties, launched in parallel with launch_runs -jobs and polled with wait_on_run and get_property PROGRESS/STATUS. This is the mode the GUI uses, and write_project_tcl emits a script that recreates the entire project from scratch.
apis.example:
create_project fpga ./fpga -part xczu7ev-ffvc1156-2-e -force
add_files [glob ./src/*.sv]
add_files -fileset constrs_1 ./constrs/top.xdc
add_files -fileset sim_1 ./tb/tb_top.sv
set_property top top [current_fileset]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
set_property STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.FLATTEN_HIERARCHY rebuilt [get_runs synth_1]
set_property strategy Performance_Explore [get_runs impl_1]
launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run impl_1
puts "impl_1 = [get_property STATUS [get_runs impl_1]]"
write_project_tcl -force ./rebuild_project.tcl

apis.name: XDC constraints
apis.description: Vivado constraints are Tcl, written in .xdc files and evaluated in order against the elaborated or synthesized netlist. They combine Synopsys SDC timing commands (create_clock, set_input_delay, set_false_path, set_multicycle_path, set_clock_groups) with Vivado-specific physical and attribute constraints expressed as set_property on design objects (PACKAGE_PIN, IOSTANDARD, LOC, ASYNC_REG, MARK_DEBUG, BITSTREAM.*). Because an XDC file is ordinary Tcl, get_* queries, foreach loops and filter expressions can be used inside it.
apis.example:
create_clock -period 10.000 -name sys_clk [get_ports clk_p]
set_input_delay  -clock sys_clk -max 2.0 [get_ports {din[*]}]
set_output_delay -clock sys_clk -max 1.5 [get_ports {dout[*]}]
set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group [get_clocks sys_clk] -group [get_clocks usb_clk]
set_false_path -from [get_ports rst_n]
set_property PACKAGE_PIN AH11 [get_ports clk_p]
set_property IOSTANDARD DIFF_SSTL12 [get_ports clk_p]
set_property ASYNC_REG true [get_cells -hier -filter {NAME =~ *sync_reg*}]

apis.name: IP Integrator block-design Tcl
apis.description: Block designs are created and wired entirely in Tcl. create_bd_design opens a canvas, create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv instantiates catalog IP by VLNV string, set_property CONFIG.* configures it, connect_bd_net and connect_bd_intf_net wire scalar and interface pins, apply_bd_automation runs the same connection rules the GUI's Run Block Automation offers, and assign_bd_address maps slaves into each master's address space. validate_bd_design checks the result, generate_target and make_wrapper produce the output products and HDL wrapper, and write_bd_tcl exports a script that rebuilds the design.
apis.example:
create_bd_design "system"
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:zynq_ultra_ps_e zynq_ultra_ps_e_0
apply_bd_automation -rule xilinx.com:bd_rule:zynq_ultra_ps_e -config {apply_board_preset "1"} [get_bd_cells zynq_ultra_ps_e_0]
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:axi_gpio axi_gpio_0
set_property -dict [list CONFIG.C_GPIO_WIDTH {8} CONFIG.C_ALL_OUTPUTS {1}] [get_bd_cells axi_gpio_0]
apply_bd_automation -rule xilinx.com:bd_rule:axi4 -config {Master "/zynq_ultra_ps_e_0/M_AXI_HPM0_FPD" Clk "Auto"} [get_bd_intf_pins axi_gpio_0/S_AXI]
assign_bd_address
validate_bd_design
save_bd_design
generate_target all [get_files system.bd]
make_wrapper -files [get_files system.bd] -top -import

apis.name: Hardware Manager Tcl
apis.description: The in-system side of the flow. open_hw_manager starts the manager, connect_hw_server attaches to a local or remote hw_server, open_hw_target selects a JTAG chain and current_hw_device picks the device. Programming is set_property PROGRAM.FILE plus program_hw_devices; debug uses PROBES.FILE with the .ltx probe file and the run_hw_ila / wait_on_hw_ila / upload_hw_ila_data / display_hw_ila_data sequence. create_hw_cfgmem and program_hw_cfgmem write configuration flash, and create_hw_axi_txn/run_hw_axi drive JTAG-to-AXI Master transactions.
apis.example:
open_hw_manager
connect_hw_server -url localhost:3121
open_hw_target
current_hw_device [lindex [get_hw_devices] 0]
set_property PROGRAM.FILE {./top.bit} [current_hw_device]
set_property PROBES.FILE  {./top.ltx} [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
refresh_hw_device [current_hw_device]
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'b1 [get_hw_probes done -of_objects [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]]
run_hw_ila [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
wait_on_hw_ila [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
display_hw_ila_data [upload_hw_ila_data [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]]

apis.name: Vitis HLS Tcl
apis.description: Vitis HLS compiles C, C++ or OpenCL into RTL. A run script opens a project, adds design and testbench files, names the top function, opens a solution, targets a part and clock, then runs C simulation (csim_design), high-level synthesis (csynth_design), C/RTL co-simulation (cosim_design) and export (export_design -format ip_catalog or -format xo). Micro-architecture is steered by #pragma HLS directives in the source (PIPELINE, UNROLL, ARRAY_PARTITION, DATAFLOW, INTERFACE, INLINE) or by equivalent set_directive_* Tcl commands kept in a directives.tcl file.
apis.example:
open_project -reset fir_prj
add_files fir.cpp
add_files -tb fir_test.cpp
set_top fir
open_solution -reset "solution1" -flow_target vivado
set_part {xcu250-figd2104-2L-e}
create_clock -period 3.33 -name default
csim_design
csynth_design
cosim_design -rtl verilog
export_design -format ip_catalog -display_name "FIR Filter"
exit

apis.name: XSCT / XSDB
apis.description: The Xilinx Software Command-Line Tool is a Tcl shell that talks to hw_server for JTAG bring-up and debug of MicroBlaze, Arm Cortex-A/R and Versal targets. Typical use is connect, select a target with targets -set -filter, download a bitstream with fpga, initialise the PS with the generated ps7_init/psu_init procedures or loadhw, download an ELF with dow, and run with con. It also scripts the classic embedded software flow (platform, domain, app projects) and reads the .xsa handoff produced by write_hw_platform.
apis.example:
connect
targets -set -nocase -filter {name =~ "*PS TAP*"}
fpga -file ./top.bit
targets -set -nocase -filter {name =~ "ARM*#0"}
loadhw -hw ./system.xsa -mem-ranges [list {0x80000000 0xbfffffff}]
rst -processor
ps7_init
ps7_post_config
dow ./hello.elf
con

apis.name: Tcl Store (tclapp)
apis.description: An open-source repository of Tcl applications that ships with Vivado and extends it with extra commands. `tclapp::list_apps` shows what is available, `tclapp::install <app>` installs one into the current session and `::tclapp::<vendor>::<app>::<proc>` calls it. The Xilinx Hub (xhub) commands manage the same content in newer releases. Useful bundled apps include designutils, projutils (export_ip_user_files, write_project_tcl helpers) and diff-based checkpoint comparison utilities.

file_formats.description: Vivado project file, an XML index beside a <project>.srcs / .runs / .cache directory tree. Opened with open_project, created with create_project and regenerated from Tcl with write_project_tcl.

Xilinx Design Constraints: Tcl source holding timing (SDC) and physical constraints. Added with read_xdc or add_files -fileset constrs_1; a single file can be scoped to synthesis only, implementation only or both via the USED_IN property.

Design checkpoint: a snapshot of the netlist, constraints and (after place/route) placement and routing. Written with write_checkpoint, reloaded with open_checkpoint or read_checkpoint + link_design, and used for incremental compile, out-of-context IP runs and hand-off between teams.

Bitstream for 7 series, UltraScale and UltraScale+ devices, produced by write_bitstream and loaded by program_hw_devices. Versal devices use a programmable device image (.pdi) written by write_device_image instead.

Raw binary bitstream and configuration-memory images. write_cfgmem converts a .bit/.pdi into flash-ready .mcs/.bin plus a .prm description for QSPI, BPI or SD boot; program_hw_cfgmem writes them to the board.

Debug probes file describing the ILA/VIO cores and the signal names attached to them. Written by write_debug_probes (or automatically by write_bitstream) and loaded into the Hardware Manager with set_property PROBES.FILE.
IP customization file holding the parameter values of one configured IP core. Created by create_ip, read with read_ip or add_files, upgraded with upgrade_ip and regenerated with generate_target.

Xilinx Shell Archive: the hardware hand-off to software tools, containing the block design, address map, driver information and optionally the bitstream. Written with write_hw_platform (-fixed -include_bit) and consumed by Vitis and XSCT (loadhw).

IP Integrator block design. Created with create_bd_design, edited with create_bd_cell/connect_bd_net, exported as a rebuild script with write_bd_tcl and turned into HDL with generate_target and make_wrapper.
XSim waveform configuration and waveform database. save_wave_config/open_wave_config manage the .wcfg view; the .wdb holds the logged simulation data produced when log_wave is active.

Build scripts, the journal of every Tcl command a session executed (vivado.jou, renamed with -journal) and the run log (vivado.log, renamed with -log). The journal is the canonical way to discover the Tcl behind a GUI action.
EDIF gate-level netlist, read with read_edif for third-party synthesis results or encrypted IP, and written with write_edif from a synthesized design.

Verilog, SystemVerilog and VHDL RTL sources, loaded with read_verilog (-sv), read_vhdl (-vhdl2008) or add_files. write_verilog and write_vhdl emit simulation or equivalence-checking netlists from a synthesized or implemented design.

Generated directory of IP simulation and synthesis support files (scripts, wrappers, memory initialisation) produced alongside a project. Regenerated with export_ip_user_files; deleting it is safe because it can always be rebuilt.
Power estimator spreadsheets and the plain-text reports written by report_timing_summary, report_utilization, report_power, report_drc and the other report_* commands with -file.
